ref: 1 Apol. 6.1 (Otto and ANF chapter 6; no subsections). Clause ends at 'καὶ τὸν τῶν'
greek: 6. Ἐνθένδε καὶ ἄθεοι κεκλήμεθα. Καὶ ὁμολογοῦμεν τῶν τοιούτων νομιζομένων Θεῶν ἄθεοι εἶναι, ἀλλ' οὐχὶ τοῦ ἀληθεστάτου καὶ πατρὸς δικαιοσύνης καὶ σωφροσύνης καὶ τῶν ἄλλων ἀρετῶν, ἀνεπιμίκτου τε κακίας Θεοῦ· ἀλλ' ἐκεῖνόν τε, καὶ τὸν παρ' αὐτοῦ υἱὸν ἐλθόντα καὶ διδάξαντα ἡμᾶς ταῦτα, καὶ τὸν τῶν
greek_edition: Otto, S. Justini philosophi et martyris opera, ed. J.C.Th. Otto, vol. 1, Jenae: Mauke 1842 (archive.org bib_fict_4102644_1). Read from the PDF text layer and checked against page images at 220 dpi; Greek shown without the apparatus superscripts. Apparatus marker ¹ after ἐλθόντα omitted.
english: Hence are we called atheists. And we confess that we are atheists, so far as gods of this sort are concerned, but not with respect to the most true God, the Father of righteousness and temperance and the other virtues, who is free from all impurity. But both Him, and the Son (who came forth from Him and taught us these things,
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe)
page: Greek: Otto 1842 p. 148 (PDF p. 228). English: page unknown (New Advent text has no ANF page numbers).
edition: Jena: Mauke, 1842 (Greek); Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (English)
what_it_says: Christians call themselves atheists only regarding the so-called gods, not regarding the most true Father and the Son who came forth from Him and taught them.
limits: Father and Son are named together as the objects of Christian acknowledgement, but 'came forth' (ἐλθόντα) is sending/teaching language and the sentence does not say what the Son is; the clause is cut in mid-sentence (the angels and Spirit follow in item 02); no homoousios or ousia language in the text.

ref: 1 Apol. 6.2 (Otto and ANF chapter 6; no subsections). Continues item 01
greek: ἄλλων ἑπομένων καὶ ἐξομοιουμένων ἀγαθῶν ἀγγέλων στρατόν, πνεῦμά τε τὸ προφητικὸν σεβόμεθα καὶ προσκυνοῦμεν, λόγῳ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ τιμῶντες καὶ παντὶ βουλομένῳ μαθεῖν, ὡς ἐδιδάχθημεν, ἀφθόνως παραδιδόντες.
greek_edition: Otto, S. Justini philosophi et martyris opera, ed. J.C.Th. Otto, vol. 1, Jenae: Mauke 1842 (archive.org bib_fict_4102644_1). Read from the PDF text layer and checked against page images at 220 dpi; Greek shown without the apparatus superscripts. Superscripts 2 and 3 (apparatus) omitted. Read as a comma after μαθεῖν (OCR layer had ';').
english: ...and the host of the other good angels who follow and are made like to Him), and the prophetic Spirit, we worship and adore, knowing them in reason and truth, and declaring without grudging to every one who wishes to learn, as we have been taught.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe)
page: Greek: Otto 1842 p. 150 (PDF p. 230). English: page unknown (New Advent text has no ANF page numbers).
edition: Jena: Mauke, 1842 (Greek); Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (English)
what_it_says: Christians worship and adore the prophetic Spirit, in reason and truth, and the host of good angels that follows the Son is named just before it.
limits: Opponents say the Spirit is placed after the angels and is only a prophetic power, and that the verbs may govern only the angels (see item 03). Justin does not say here that Spirit is God. The English 'worship and adore' is the ANF rendering of σεβόμεθα καὶ προσκυνοῦμεν, which the Greek applies to the Spirit in this clause and possibly to the angels too.

ref: 1 Apol. 6, Otto's apparatus on 'ἀγγέλων στρατόν' and 'ταῦτα' (Latin notes)
greek: Langus, Grabius et Thalemannus jungunt cum διδάξαντα, ut Christus non homines modo, sed etiam angelos docuisse dicatur; Roesslerus et Moehlerus copulant ἀγγέλ. στρ. et ταῦτα cum διδάξαντα: Filius Dei nos non solum de his, sed etiam de angelis edocuit; Keilius mavult στρατηγόν pro στρατόν, ut Christus dux angelorum appelletur; Neander, Georgii et Hasselbach verba καὶ τὸν τῶν ἄλλων... στρατόν ita pendere censent a σεβόμεθα καὶ προσκυνοῦμεν, ut revera de angelorum cultu disseratur. Ταῦτα autem non referendum est ad id, quod antea de paganis daemonibus, sed ad id, quod modo de veri Dei attributis (δικαιοσ. καὶ σωφροσ. etc.) erat expositum.
greek_edition: Otto, S. Justini philosophi et martyris opera, ed. J.C.Th. Otto, vol. 1, Jenae: Mauke 1842 (archive.org bib_fict_4102644_1). Read from the PDF text layer and checked against page images at 220 dpi; Greek shown without the apparatus superscripts. This is Otto's Latin note (secondary source), read from the page image.
translator: n/a (Otto's Latin note; Latin secondary source)
page: Otto 1842 p. 149 (PDF p. 229), note on p. 149 bottom. English: page unknown (New Advent text has no ANF page numbers).
edition: Jena: Mauke, 1842 (Greek); Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (English)
what_it_says: Otto lists the nineteenth-century readings of the angel clause and his own view that 'these things' refer to the attributes of the true God, not to the demons.
limits: Otto does not argue the Trinitarian point; the 'angelic worship' reading is reported as held by Neander, Georgii and Hasselbach. Keil's reading στρατηγόν would make the Son 'leader of the angels', a different Christology. Otto's citation of his own book (De Justini Martyris scriptis et doctrina p. 143 sqq.) was not consulted.

ref: 1 Apol. 6, Otto's apparatus notes 2 and 3 on 'προσκυνοῦμεν' and 'ὡς ἐδιδάχθημεν'
greek: 2. προσκυν. λόγῳ κ. ἀληθ. τιμ.] Coll. ev. Joann. IV. 24. 3. ὡς ἐδιδ.] Erunt fortasse qui omnino legendum putent ὅσα; nos nihil mutamus. Thirlbius.
greek_edition: Otto, S. Justini philosophi et martyris opera, ed. J.C.Th. Otto, vol. 1, Jenae: Mauke 1842 (archive.org bib_fict_4102644_1). Read from the PDF text layer and checked against page images at 220 dpi; Greek shown without the apparatus superscripts. Note text read from the page image.
translator: n/a (Otto's apparatus; Greek and Latin secondary source)
page: Otto 1842 p. 150 (PDF p. 230), notes at foot of page. English: page unknown (New Advent text has no ANF page numbers).
edition: Jena: Mauke, 1842 (Greek); Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (English)
what_it_says: Otto cites John 4:24 as a parallel to 'worship in reason and truth' and notes a proposal to read ὅσα for ὡς ἐδιδάχθημεν, which he does not adopt.
limits: The John 4:24 reference is Otto's only; I did not open the Johannine text in this run, and the parallel does not itself state a Trinity. The ὅσα variant does not affect the Trinitarian sense.

ref: 1 Apol. 13.1 (Otto and ANF chapter 13; no subsections). Greek starts at 'Τὸν διδάσκαλόν'
greek: Τὸν διδάσκαλόν τε τούτων γενόμενον ἡμῖν καὶ εἰς τοῦτο γεννηθέντα Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, τὸν σταυρωθέντα ἐπὶ Ποντίου Πιλάτου, τοῦ γενομένου ἐν Ἰουδαίᾳ ἐπὶ χρόνοις Τιβερίου Καίσαρος ἐπιτρόπου, υἱὸν αὐτοῦ τοῦ ὄντως θεοῦ μαθόντες καὶ ἐν δευτέρᾳ χώρᾳ ἔχοντες, πνεῦμά τε προφητικὸν ἐν τρίτῃ τάξει ὅτι μετὰ λόγου τιμῶμεν, ἀποδείξομεν.
greek_edition: Otto, S. Justini philosophi et martyris opera, ed. J.C.Th. Otto, vol. 1, Jenae: Mauke 1842 (archive.org bib_fict_4102644_1). Read from the PDF text layer and checked against page images at 220 dpi; Greek shown without the apparatus superscripts. Superscripts 3 and 4 omitted. Words 'ὅτι μετὰ λόγου τιμῶμεν' have no quotation marks in this print (the OCR layer had them).
english: Our teacher of these things is Jesus Christ, who also was born for this purpose, and was crucified under Pontius Pilate, procurator of Judæa, in the times of Tiberius Cæsar; and that we reasonably worship Him, having learned that He is the Son of the true God Himself, and holding Him in the second place, and the prophetic Spirit in the third, we will prove.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe)
page: Greek: Otto 1842 p. 164 (PDF p. 244). English: page unknown (New Advent text has no ANF page numbers).
edition: Jena: Mauke, 1842 (Greek); Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (English)
what_it_says: Justin says Christians worship Jesus as the Son of the true God, placing Him second and the prophetic Spirit third.
limits: This is the text opponents cite for ranked 'second place' and 'third rank'. Justin does not explain how the ranks relate to the Father's nature. 'Second place' (δευτέρᾳ χώρᾳ) is an explicit ordering. The 'worship' is grounded in the claim of sonship, not in a claim of equal God.

ref: 1 Apol. 13.2 (Otto and ANF chapter 13; no subsections)
greek: Ἐνταῦθα γὰρ μανίαν ἡμῶν καταφαίνονται, δευτέραν χώραν μετὰ τὸν ἄτρεπτον καὶ ἀεὶ ὄντα θεὸν καὶ γεννήτορα τὸν ἁπάντων ἀνθρώπῳ σταυρωθέντι διδόναι ἡμᾶς λέγοντες, ἀγνοοῦντες τὸ ἐν τούτῳ μυστήριον, ᾧ προσέχειν ὑμᾶς ἐξηγουμένων ἡμῶν προτρεπόμεθα.
greek_edition: Otto, S. Justini philosophi et martyris opera, ed. J.C.Th. Otto, vol. 1, Jenae: Mauke 1842 (archive.org bib_fict_4102644_1). Read from the PDF text layer and checked against page images at 220 dpi; Greek shown without the apparatus superscripts.
english: For they proclaim our madness to consist in this, that we give to a crucified man a place second to the unchangeable and eternal God, the Creator of all; for they do not discern the mystery that is herein, to which, as we make it plain to you, we pray you to give heed.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe)
page: Greek: Otto 1842 p. 164 (PDF p. 244). English: page unknown (New Advent text has no ANF page numbers).
edition: Jena: Mauke, 1842 (Greek); Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (English)
what_it_says: Justin answers that critics object to giving the crucified man the second place after the unchangeable, eternal God and Creator of all, and that they miss a mystery he will explain.
limits: Justin declares the mystery but does not state it here (he defers the explanation). The text says 'second place after the unchangeable God and begetter of all' as an accusation by critics, so the second place is itself conceded by Justin. The critics' point is about the crucified man, not about the Spirit.

ref: 1 Apol. 13, Otto's apparatus notes 3, 4 and 6 on 'υἱὸν αὐτοῦ τοῦ ὄντως θεοῦ', 'μετὰ λόγου', 'γεννήτορα τὸν ἁπάντων'
greek: 3. υἱὸν αὐτοῦ τοῦ ὄντως θεοῦ] Thirlb. frustra commendat υἱὸν αὐτὸν τοῦ ὄντος ὄντος θεοῦ. 4. μετὰ λόγου] Fortasse μετὰ (τὸν) λόγον ... praesertim quum statim sequatur: μετὰ τὸν ἄτρεπτον κ. ἀ. ὄ. θεόν. Sed nihil mutamus. 6. γεννήτορα τὸν ἁπάντων] Notat Sylburg. cuipiam fortasse legendum videri τῶν πάντων, sed probe addit, illam quoque constructionem in Justino saepius occurrere.
greek_edition: Otto, S. Justini philosophi et martyris opera, ed. J.C.Th. Otto, vol. 1, Jenae: Mauke 1842 (archive.org bib_fict_4102644_1). Read from the PDF text layer and checked against page images at 220 dpi; Greek shown without the apparatus superscripts. Note 3 partly illegible at 220 dpi; the 'ὄντος ὄντος' reading is partly OCR-assisted.
translator: n/a (Otto's apparatus; Greek and Latin secondary source)
page: Otto 1842 p. 164 (PDF p. 244), notes at foot of page. English: page unknown (New Advent text has no ANF page numbers).
edition: Jena: Mauke, 1842 (Greek); Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (English)
what_it_says: Otto keeps the printed text in each case: Thirlby's variant for 'the truly existing God', a possible μετὰ (τὸν) λόγον, and Sylburg's possible τῶν πάντων in place of τὸν ἁπάντων.
limits: These are textual doubts, not opponents' arguments. Otto does not adopt any variant. Sylburg's suggestion would change 'begetter of all' (Father) into a different construction. Partial legibility means item 07 is PARTLY verified.

ref: 1 Apol. 21 (Otto and ANF chapter 21; no subsections). Greek cut at 'τὸν δι-'
greek: 21. Τῷ δὲ καὶ τὸν λόγον, ὅ ἐστι πρῶτον γέννημα τοῦ θεοῦ, ἄνευ ἐπιμιξίας φάσκειν ἡμᾶς γεγενῆσθαι, Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν τὸν δι-
greek_edition: Otto, S. Justini philosophi et martyris opera, ed. J.C.Th. Otto, vol. 1, Jenae: Mauke 1842 (archive.org bib_fict_4102644_1). Read from the PDF text layer and checked against page images at 220 dpi; Greek shown without the apparatus superscripts. Line cut where the page image was checked. Apparatus note 1 ('γεγενῆσθαι': Thirlby would read γεγεννῆσθαι) read only from the OCR layer on PDF p. 261, not checked by image.
english: And when we say also that the Word, who is the first-birth of God, was produced without sexual union, and that He, Jesus Christ, our Teacher, was crucified and died, and rose again, and ascended into heaven, we propound nothing different from what you believe regarding those whom you esteem sons of Jupiter.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe)
page: Greek: Otto 1842 p. 180 (PDF p. 260). English: page unknown (New Advent text has no ANF page numbers).
edition: Jena: Mauke, 1842 (Greek); Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (English)
what_it_says: Justin says the Word, the first offspring of God, was produced without sexual union, and he compares this with the pagan sons of Jupiter.
limits: The verb 'was produced' (γεγενῆσθαι) and 'first offspring' (πρῶτον γέννημα) are the words opponents use for temporal generation. Justin gives no date and no metaphysics here. The pagan comparison is his defence, and it is itself an analogy, not a doctrine.

ref: 1 Apol. 21 (Otto and ANF chapter 21; list of pagan sons of Jupiter)
greek: Πόσους γὰρ υἱοὺς φάσκουσι τοῦ Διὸς οἱ παρ' ὑμῖν τιμώμενοι συγγραφεῖς, ἐπίστασθε· Ἑρμὴν μέν, λόγον τὸν ἑρμηνευτικὸν καὶ πάντων διδάσκαλον, Ἀσκληπιὸν δὲ καὶ θεραπευτὴν γενόμενον, κεραυνωθέντα ἀνεληλυθέναι εἰς οὐρανόν,
greek_edition: Otto, S. Justini philosophi et martyris opera, ed. J.C.Th. Otto, vol. 1, Jenae: Mauke 1842 (archive.org bib_fict_4102644_1). Read from the PDF text layer and checked against page images at 220 dpi; Greek shown without the apparatus superscripts. Superscripts 2 and 3 omitted.
english: For you know how many sons your esteemed writers ascribed to Jupiter: Mercury, the interpreting word and teacher of all; Æsculapius, who, though he was a great physician, was struck by a thunderbolt, and so ascended to heaven;
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe)
page: Greek: Otto 1842 p. 182 (PDF p. 262). English: page unknown (New Advent text has no ANF page numbers).
edition: Jena: Mauke, 1842 (Greek); Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (English)
what_it_says: Justin names Hermes (Mercury) as the 'interpreting word and teacher of all' among the pagan sons of Jupiter.
limits: The Logos/Hermes parallel is the basis of the 'angelic Logos' charge (item 11). Justin presents the pagan list as the opponents' own, so it is an argumentum ad hominem rather than his doctrine.

ref: 1 Apol. 22 (Otto and ANF chapter 22; no subsections)
greek: 22. Υἱὸς δὲ Θεοῦ ὁ Ἰησοῦς λεγόμενος, εἰ καὶ κοινῶς μόνον ἄνθρωπος, διὰ σοφίαν ἄξιος υἱὸς Θεοῦ λέγεσθαι· πατέρα γὰρ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε πάντες συγγραφεῖς τὸν Θεὸν καλοῦσιν.
greek_edition: Otto, S. Justini philosophi et martyris opera, ed. J.C.Th. Otto, vol. 1, Jenae: Mauke 1842 (archive.org bib_fict_4102644_1). Read from the PDF text layer and checked against page images at 220 dpi; Greek shown without the apparatus superscripts. Superscripts 1 and 2 omitted.
english: Moreover, the Son of God called Jesus, even if only a man by ordinary generation, yet, on account of His wisdom, is worthy to be called the Son of God; for all writers call God the Father of men and gods.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe)
page: Greek: Otto 1842 p. 184 (PDF p. 264). English: page unknown (New Advent text has no ANF page numbers).
edition: Jena: Mauke, 1842 (Greek); Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (English)
what_it_says: Justin concedes that Jesus is by ordinary generation only a man, but says He is called Son of God because of His wisdom, as the pagan writers call God the Father of men and gods.
limits: This is the Unitarian/Ebionite-style reading: sonship by wisdom and ordinary generation. Justin's 'if only' (εἰ καὶ κοινῶς μόνον) is a conditional, not a denial. The following sentence (item 11) gives his real claim.

ref: 1 Apol. 22 (Otto and ANF chapter 22; no subsections). Continues item 10
greek: Εἰ δὲ καὶ ἰδίως παρὰ τὴν κοινὴν γένεσιν γεγεννῆσθαι αὐτὸν ἐκ Θεοῦ λέγομεν λόγον Θεοῦ, ὡς προέφημεν, κοινὸν τοῦτο ἔστω ὑμῖν τοῖς τὸν Ἑρμῆν λόγον τὸν παρὰ Θεοῦ ἀγγελτικὸν λέγουσιν.
greek_edition: Otto, S. Justini philosophi et martyris opera, ed. J.C.Th. Otto, vol. 1, Jenae: Mauke 1842 (archive.org bib_fict_4102644_1). Read from the PDF text layer and checked against page images at 220 dpi; Greek shown without the apparatus superscripts. Form 'γεγεννῆσθαι' read from the image; check at higher dpi (see notes.md).
english: And if we assert that the Word of God was born of God in a peculiar manner, different from ordinary generation, let this, as said above, be no extraordinary thing to you, who say that Mercury is the angelic word of God.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe)
page: Greek: Otto 1842 p. 184 (PDF p. 264). English: page unknown (New Advent text has no ANF page numbers).
edition: Jena: Mauke, 1842 (Greek); Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (English)
what_it_says: Justin says the Word was born from God in a manner peculiar to Himself, unlike ordinary generation, and that the pagans who call Hermes God's angelic word should accept this.
limits: 'Peculiar' (ἰδίως) supports a non-ordinary generation, but the comparison with the angelic Hermes-word is the basis of the charge that the Logos is an angel (items 09, 15 of the brief). Justin does not say here whether the generation is eternal or in time.

ref: 1 Apol. 23 (Otto and ANF chapter 23; no subsections). Greek begins 'καὶ Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς'
greek: καὶ Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς μόνος ἰδίως υἱὸς τῷ θεῷ γεγέννηται, λόγος αὐτοῦ ὑπάρχων καὶ πρωτότοκος καὶ δύναμις, καὶ τῇ βουλῇ αὐτοῦ γενόμενος ἄνθρωπος ταῦτα ἡμᾶς ἐδίδαξεν ἐπ' ἀλλαγῇ καὶ ἐπαναγωγῇ τοῦ ἀνθρωπείου γένους·
greek_edition: Otto, S. Justini philosophi et martyris opera, ed. J.C.Th. Otto, vol. 1, Jenae: Mauke 1842 (archive.org bib_fict_4102644_1). Read from the PDF text layer and checked against page images at 220 dpi; Greek shown without the apparatus superscripts.
english: (secondly) that Jesus Christ is the only proper Son who has been begotten by God, being His Word and first-begotten, and power; and, becoming man according to His will, He taught us these things for the conversion and restoration of the human race
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe)
page: Greek: Otto 1842 p. 186 (PDF p. 266). English: page unknown (New Advent text has no ANF page numbers).
edition: Jena: Mauke, 1842 (Greek); Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (English)
what_it_says: Justin says Jesus Christ is the only proper Son begotten by God, being God's Word, first-begotten and power, who became man by God's will.
limits: 'Power' (δύναμις) is also a title here, which the 'power of God' reading (Spirit as a power) can use. 'By His will' (τῇ βουλῇ) is the Arian proof-text. The text does not say co-eternal or of the same substance. It does say 'only proper Son' (μόνος ἰδίως υἱός).

ref: 1 Apol. 26 (Otto and ANF chapter 26; no subsections). Simon and Helena
greek: ΣΙΜΩΝΙ ΔΕΩ ΣΑΓΚΤΩ. Καὶ σχεδὸν πάντες μὲν Σαμαρεῖς, ὀλίγοι δὲ καὶ ἐν ἄλλοις ἔθνεσιν, ὡς τὸν πρῶτον θεὸν ἐκεῖνον ὁμολογοῦντες, ἐκεῖνον καὶ προσκυνοῦσι. Καὶ Ἑλένην τινά, τὴν περινοστήσασαν αὐτῷ κατ' ἐκεῖνο τοῦ καιροῦ, πρότερον ἐπὶ τέγους σταθεῖσαν, τὴν ἀπ' αὐτοῦ ἔννοιαν πρώτην γενομένην λέγουσι.
greek_edition: Otto, S. Justini philosophi et martyris opera, ed. J.C.Th. Otto, vol. 1, Jenae: Mauke 1842 (archive.org bib_fict_4102644_1). Read from the PDF text layer and checked against page images at 220 dpi; Greek shown without the apparatus superscripts. The Latin inscription appears in Greek capitals in the print.
english: in the language of Rome: — Simoni Deo Sancto, To Simon the holy God. And almost all the Samaritans, and a few even of other nations, worship him, and acknowledge him as the first god; and a woman, Helena, who went about with him at that time, and had formerly been a prostitute, they say is the first idea generated by him.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe)
page: Greek: Otto 1842 p. 192 (PDF p. 272). English: page unknown (New Advent text has no ANF page numbers).
edition: Jena: Mauke, 1842 (Greek); Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (English)
what_it_says: Justin reports that Samaritans worship Simon as the first god and call Helena, his companion, his first Ennoia (thought).
limits: This is Justin's report of Simon's followers, not his doctrine. 'The first god' and 'first idea' are the vocabulary of Simonian and later Gnostic systems; they show that Justin reads 'first' language against the heretics, not that his Logos is a 'first thought'. The English 'Simoni Deo Sancto' is ANF's translation of the Greek-letter Latin inscription.

ref: 1 Apol. 26 (Otto and ANF chapter 26; no subsections). Menander and Marcion
greek: Μένανδρον δέ τινα, καὶ αὐτὸν Σαμαρέα τὸν ἀπὸ κώμης Καππαρεταίας, γενόμενον μαθητὴν τοῦ Σίμωνος, ἐνεργηθέντα καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν δαιμονίων καὶ ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ γενόμενον πολλοὺς ἐξαπατῆσαι διὰ μαγικῆς τέχνης οἴδαμεν· ὃς καὶ τοὺς αὐτῷ ἑπομένους ὡς μηδὲ ἀποθνήσκοιεν ἔπεισε, καὶ νῦν εἰσί τινες ἀπ᾽ ἐκείνου τοῦτο ὁμολογοῦντες. Μαρκίωνα δέ τινα Ποντικόν, ὃς καὶ νῦν ἔτι ἐστὶ διδάσκων τοὺς πειθομένους, ἄλλον τινὰ νομίζειν μείζονα τοῦ δημιουργοῦ θεόν,
greek_edition: Otto, S. Justini philosophi et martyris opera, ed. J.C.Th. Otto, vol. 1, Jenae: Mauke 1842 (archive.org bib_fict_4102644_1). Read from the PDF text layer and checked against page images at 220 dpi; Greek shown without the apparatus superscripts. Superscripts omitted.
english: And a man, Menander, also a Samaritan, of the town Capparetæa, a disciple of Simon, and inspired by devils, we know to have deceived many while he was in Antioch by his magical art. He persuaded those who adhered to him that they should never die, and even now there are some living who hold this opinion of his. And there is Marcion, a man of Pontus, who is even at this day alive, and teaching his disciples to believe in some other god greater than the Creator.
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe)

edition: Jena: Mauke, 1842 (Greek); Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (English)
what_it_says: Justin condemns Menander and Marcion: Menander's followers were promised they would never die, and Marcion teaches his disciples to believe in another god greater than the Creator.
limits: This is the key contrast for the 'another God' charge (heteros theos). Justin's Logos is 'second' and subordinate to the Father, not 'another God greater than the Creator'; but the text does not spell out that difference. Opponents will say the words 'another god' appear in the same book.

greek: παρ' ἡμῖν λεγόμενον Χριστόν, ἄνθρωπον ἐξ ἀνθρώπων ὄντα, μαγικῇ τέχνῃ ἃς λέγομεν δυνάμεις πεποιηκέναι καὶ δόξαι διὰ τοῦτο υἱὸν θεοῦ εἶναι, τὴν ἀπόδειξιν ἤδη ποιησόμεθα, οὐ τοῖς λέγουσι πιστεύοντες, ἀλλὰ τοῖς προφητεύουσι πρὶν ἢ γενέσθαι κατ' ἀνάγκην πειθόμενοι

english: But lest any one should meet us with the question, What should prevent that He whom we call Christ, being a man born of men, performed what we call His mighty works by magical art, and by this appeared to be the Son of God? We will now offer proof, not trusting mere assertions, but being of necessity persuaded by those who prophesied [of Him] before these things came to pass
translator: Marcus Dods and George Reith (ANF vol. 1, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe)
page: Greek: Otto 1842 p. 200 (PDF p. 280). English: page unknown (New Advent text has no ANF page numbers).
edition: Jena: Mauke, 1842 (Greek); Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (English)
what_it_says: Justin answers the charge that Christ was a man who was merely a magician and was called Son of God by his magic: the proof is the fulfilment of prophecy, not assertion.
limits: The 'Son of God' title is here asserted as the claim the magic-charge targets; Justin does not explain the sonship in this chapter. The text is a defence of Christ's divine sonship by prophecy, not of the Trinity.
